newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: "Rush crops" slash prices at Colombo tea auction.
newsitem.headline: "Rush crops" slash prices at Colombo tea auction.

text.p: Lower quality teas pushed prices down at the Colombo auction on Wednesday where a high quantity of 5.8 million kg was on offer, brokers said.

"Prices came down this week due to low quality," said Rohan Iddawela of brokers Forbes and Walker. "Rush crops are coming into the market these days, where quantity is boosted by rain but quality is lowered."
Most varieties of the island's distinct low growns, popular with Russian and Middle Eastern buyers, were down. Most leafy grades lost three to six rupee per kg and more, Forbes said.
Many high growns held firm while others in the better category were irregularly lower by three to four rupees. CTC teas were also lower by two to five rupees all round.
The anticipated average auction price for the 5.8 million kg on offer was 112 rupees ($1.91) per kg as against 115.80 rupees last week, Forbes said in a report.
Iddawela said rush crops would continue to bring prices down for the next few weeks, before the Uva quality season set in towards the end of August to brighten up the sales.
The next auction is on July 15-16 when 5.9 million kg will be on offer. ($=58.46)
